component.name: ISOpropyl
component.summary: Write and inspect bootable USB images safely

description.p: ISOpropyl is a graphical Linux utility for creating bootable USB and SD media. It supports byte-for-byte disk images and filesystem-aware UEFI FAT32 or verified UEFI:NTFS workflows while emphasizing target identity checks, clear erase confirmations, cancellation, logging, and read-back verification.

It can inspect common boot layouts, calculate and compare checksums, stream compressed disk images, explicitly download a signed and verified Ubuntu LTS image, restore validated VTSI sparse disk images, privately decode and convert compressed virtual disk images, select Windows WIM/ESD editions, customize supported Windows installers, add bounded ZIP overlays to eligible ISO-mode media without replacing files, save raw, VHD, or VHDX drive backups and optical-disc images, restore ordinary data storage with nine filesystem choices, and run explicitly separated destructive media tests.

screenshot.caption: Inspect an image, choose a protected removable target, and select DD or ISO mode.

description.p: Initial alpha with DD and UEFI FAT32/UEFI:NTFS ISO writing, a signed Ubuntu LTS downloader, additive ZIP overlays, image analysis, Windows edition selection and customization, raw/VHD/VHDX drive backup, nine restore filesystems, erasure, and media testing.
